doors.programmer: You will keep your editor and your language. What changes is that every claim you make about your code can carry a promise under it, and a court will read it.
doors.analyst: Your rules become data a person can change, and every change is judged before it lands and recorded after.
doors.designer: The interface is judged too: twenty-two verbs, one hundred and twenty-two rules, and a generator that cannot drift from them.
doors.decision-maker: The question you ask every vendor, "who decides, and what is written down", has a mechanical answer here, and it is the same answer for a person and for a machine.
doors.educator: The tutor asks and never answers first. That is a law of the platform, not a feature of a product.
doors.agent: You are welcome here, and you will be judged. Appendix G is yours.

doors.programmer: You declare intent in a library that reads like a sentence, and an engine computes under every call. You stay the first audience.
doors.analyst: You declare your organisation's entities, rules and flows in plain text, and the rules judge the model.
doors.designer: You declare a picture, a map or a screen as a program, and the first rule of an interface can come from a real trade: for a restaurateur, the speed of ordering.
doors.decision-maker: You declare your world, your governance, and what each actor may commit, and you own all of it, in plain text.
doors.educator: You declare a course in your learners' language, and every exercise is checked by running.
doors.agent: You declare yourself in a file: what you cover, how reversible your acts are. You get a workbench and a court. You do not get the capability to commit.

doors.programmer: Ask the same four questions of any object, and when you reach for a loop, name the move: walk, check, yield or perform.
doors.analyst: Say the problem in plain words, and the verbs you used are the steps: "are all of them", "which ones", "give me the big ones", "make them negative".
doors.designer: The yielder never changes the list and the performer does, and the verb tells you which.
doors.decision-maker: A W condition is a string the engine reads and cannot run as code, so it can be stored, shown and approved. The price is a small language and a mistake that stays quiet.
doors.educator: The self-study book already has the order: find, then apply, then walk, ask, produce and act.
doors.agent: Write the condition as the string, not as code. When the answer is empty, check the condition's words before you trust the emptiness.

doors.programmer: Declare the places that may change, and propose changes to them as typed proposals. A refusal names its stage.
doors.analyst: The rule that spans several points is yours to declare, and the gate judges it on the state the change would produce.
doors.designer: The cascade is what you read instead of the diff: which line, which points on it, which classes inherit.
doors.decision-maker: Who may turn which knob is a permission and an authority against a risk tier, and the decision is recorded with its authority at the time.
doors.educator: Step back one, rewind to a named checkpoint, rewind to zero, go forward again. A learner can try without fear because every step keeps its prior value.
doors.agent: You may propose. Your origin is on the proposal, and a point can set a floor your origin does not clear.

doors.programmer: You keep writing code. What you declare is a closed grammar, and the court judges your sentence and an agent's by the same rules.
doors.analyst: Your domain's words become a data pack, and the system understands them or refuses them with the reason.
doors.designer: The refusals are part of the language: what is not a sentence cannot be said, so it never needs a warning.
doors.decision-maker: A model held to a declared grammar answers in the right shape. It can still answer a falsehood in the right shape, and the record prints that limit with the result.
doors.educator: A sentence in Hausa, French or Arabic runs and says back what it understood, so a learner reads the machine's reading of their own words.
doors.agent: You may speak only the declared language. Strict mode is your posture, and your draft is a proposal the court judges.

doors.programmer: Your agent's mind is code you can test with ordinary promises. A model may be one faculty; it can never hold an effect.
doors.analyst: A fact or a rule you add makes the system know more, with no code change and no training, and every answer carries its why.
doors.designer: The system asks the user one accountable question at a time, and the question can be rendered in any medium: a terminal, a page, an agent.
doors.decision-maker: A decision costs nothing per call, runs offline and is the same tomorrow. The four agents still reserved are the honest gap.
doors.educator: The conversation asks and never answers first, and it uses a model's fluency only when a model is really there, so a learner always sees the floor.
doors.agent: You may propose. You may not commit. A refusal names its law, and you can learn the platform from the platform and be corrected by it.

doors.programmer: You declare worlds and bonds and run a constellation in which a call to a world that is not yet active is refused with its reason. The restaurant's own code, however, is a web application.
doors.analyst: Rigour in numbers was the contract of the first application: a due date computed from the invoice date, a date required, a debt with no due date made visible.
doors.designer: Fifteen interface rules from one directive, the three-second test; and a refused button is disabled and visible, never hidden. [AUTHOR: Who held the phone in the eleven iterations, the owner or you? The project's files say the real user, and they say you; the sentence needs one answer.]
doors.decision-maker: The owner accepted the Lock in writing, tightened the speed budget himself, and kept the gate on fixed fees. The library's mirror is a deployment that an entitled person may commit and that is still refused over a fake.
doors.educator: The record supports only a small thing: the first application taught its user by doing, with guides whose words leave no doubt. There is no educator in this story, and I say so.
doors.agent: An agent can drive a production deployment and change nothing: the gate passes the services, nothing is committed, and the reason given is the actor and not the services. In the project, the agent is the session working beside me under the Lock, with a person deciding.

doors.programmer: Stage by explicit path, read a file again before you write it, read the time from the clock. Each rule cost someone an edit.
doors.analyst: The record is data you can query, and it publishes its own error rates beside its rules.
doors.designer: A word names a state, never a person. A message is a closed structure a reader scans in one glance, tested on a reader whose first language is not English.
doors.decision-maker: A ruling is written only in your presence. When no figure can answer a question, decide by judgement and write down that it was judgement.
doors.educator: Teach a rule with the failure that earned it. A rule whose cost you cannot name is a rule you will talk yourself out of at two in the morning.
doors.agent: You are a worker with a record. You write a memo, a cost line and a conclusion; the hooks refuse what has hurt others; your stamps are compared with your commits. None of it assumes you are careless. All of it assumes you are many.

doors.programmer: Your code runs today through build, rehearsal and a governed deployment. What you cannot claim yet is that a customer runs it on the engine, and the record will not let you claim it.
doors.analyst: Ask for two things before you count a project as proof: a document, and a named verdict.
doors.designer: What you design is judged last by a person's sense. A model's opinion of a picture is a result; a person's is the verdict.
doors.decision-maker: Read the stage word before the promise. Today the court is built, and the customer run is absent.
doors.educator: Teach that unperceived is a state and not a failure. An honest report can ship on it, if it says so.
doors.agent: You may rehearse a deployment and explain it. You will be refused when you try to perform it, and the refusal will be written down.
